items.title: Light-Perception Unpacked in Full: Eleven Obstacles Across Reflection and Cultivation

items.zh: 又第一義思所成慧及修所成慧俱光明想，有十一法為所對治。云何十一？謂思所成慧俱光明想有四法，修所成慧俱光明想有七法。如是所治，合有十一。
items.en: In terms of the ultimate truth, light-perception joined with reflection-wisdom and with cultivation-wisdom has eleven things to be remedied. What are the eleven? Four belong to light-perception joined with reflection-wisdom, and seven belong to light-perception joined with cultivation-wisdom. Thus the things to be remedied number eleven in all.

items.zh: 思所成慧俱光明想有四法者，一、不善觀察故，不善決定故，於所思惟有疑隨逐。二、住於夜分，嬾惰懈怠故，多習睡眠故，虛度時分。三、住於晝分，習近邪惡食故，身不調柔，不能隨順諦觀諸法。四、與在家、出家共相雜住，於隨所聞所究竟法，不能如理作意思惟。如是疑隨逐故，障礙能遣疑因緣故；此四種法，是思所成慧俱光明想之所對治，令思所成若智、若見不得清淨。何等名為修所成慧俱光明想所治七法？一、依舉相修，極勇精進所對治法。二、依止相修，極劣精進所對治法。三、依捨相修，貪著定味與愛俱行所有喜悅。四、於般涅槃心懷恐怖，與瞋恚俱其心怯弱，二所治法。五、即依如是方便作意，於法精勤論議決擇，於立破門多生言論，相續不捨。此於寂靜正思惟時，能為障礙。六、於色聲香味觸中，不如正理執取相好，不正尋思，令心散亂。七、於不應思處，強攝其心思擇諸法。如是七種，是修所成慧俱光明想所對治法，極能障礙修所成慧俱光明想，令修所成若知、若見不清淨轉。此所治法，還有十一與此相違能對治法，能斷於彼，當知亦令思修所成若知、若見清淨而轉。又正方便修諸想者，有能斷滅所治法欲。又於所治現行法中，心不染著，速令斷滅。又能多住能對治法，斷滅一切所對治法。如是三法，隨逐一切對治修故，名多所作。如是名為修習對治。此修對治，當知即是修習瑜伽。此第五支修習對治廣聖教義，當知唯有如是十相。除此更無若過若增。

items.title: The Sixth Branch Opens: Mundane Purity, and the Three Stages of Genuine Meditative Mastery

items.zh: 云何世間一切種清淨？當知略有三種。一、得三摩地，二、三摩地圓滿，三、三摩地自在。
items.en: What is mundane purity of every kind? It should be known, in brief, to be threefold: attaining concentration, perfecting concentration, and mastery over concentration.

items.title: Twenty Obstacles Between a Practitioner and Genuine Concentration

items.zh: 此中最初有二十種得三摩地所對治法，能令不得勝三摩地。
items.en: At the outset there are twenty things to be remedied that can prevent one from attaining excellent concentration.

items.zh: 何等二十？一、有不樂斷同梵行者為伴過失。二、伴雖有德，然能宣說修定方便師有過失。謂顛倒說修定方便。三、師雖有德，然於所說修定方便，其能聽者欲樂羸劣，心散亂故，不能領受過失。四、其能聽者雖有樂欲，屬耳而聽；然闇鈍故，覺慧劣故，不能領受過失。五、雖有智德，然是愛行，多求利養恭敬過失。六、多分憂愁，難養難滿，不知喜足過失。七、即由如是增上力故，多諸事務過失。八、雖無此失，然有懈怠嬾惰故，棄捨加行過失。九、雖無此失，然有為他種種障礙生起過失。十、雖無此失，然有於寒熱等苦，不能堪忍過失。十一、雖無此失，然有慢恚過故，不能領受教誨過失。十二、雖無此失，然有於教顛倒思惟過失。十三、雖無此失，然於所受教有忘念過失。十四、雖無此失，然有在家、出家雜住過失。十五、雖無此失，然有受用五失相應臥具過失。五失相應臥具，應知如聲聞地當說。十六、雖無此失，然於遠離處不守護諸根故，有不正尋思過失。十七、雖無此失，然由食不平等故，有身沈重無所堪能過失。十八、雖無此失，然性多睡眠，有多睡眠隨煩惱現行過失。十九、雖無此失，然不先修行奢摩他品故，於內心寂止遠離中，有不欣樂過失。二十、雖無此失，然先不修行毘鉢舍那品故，於增上慧法毘鉢舍那如實觀中，有不欣樂過失。如是二十種法，是奢摩他、毘鉢舍那品，證得心一境性之所對治。

blocks.text: The fifth branch closes with the obstacles to light-perception; the sixth branch, **mundane purity**, opens. Two long lists are **untranslated** (0390c15–0391a16 and 0391a20–b20); the commentary summarises them.

There are eleven: four for light-perception joined with wisdom from reflection, seven for that joined with wisdom from cultivation. Master Cháng Bǎi: before calm and insight are achieved, it is not yet wisdom from cultivation.

The untranslated list: at the **reflection** stage, (1) doubt from poor examination; (2) wasting the night in sleep; (3) by day, unsuitable food leaving the body heavy; (4) living among others so one cannot reflect properly. At the **cultivation** stage, (1) excessive effort while rousing the mind; (2) too little effort while calming it; (3) attachment to the joy of concentration while in equanimity; (4) fear of nirvāṇa and timid aversion; (5) endless debate about the teaching when one should be quietly reflecting; (6) grasping at the features of sense objects; (7) forcing the mind to think about what should not be thought about. Eleven contrary practices remedy them. The whole fifth branch is, in fact, "the cultivation of yoga".

Mundane purity is threefold: **attaining concentration**, **perfecting** it, and **mastery** over it. Master Cháng Bǎi: attaining concentration means reaching access concentration. Non-Buddhists also have the absorptions, but they do not attend to mastery or to removing the subtle afflictions within them.

(Untranslated.) Companions who do not wish to give up the household life; a teacher who explains the method wrongly; a listener who lacks interest, or is too dull to understand; craving for gain and honour; discontent and being hard to support; too many affairs; laziness; obstacles caused by others; inability to bear cold and heat; pride or anger that refuses instruction; misunderstanding instructions; forgetting them; living among householders and monastics; using unsuitable lodgings; unguarded senses; immoderate eating; too much sleep; no prior practice of calm, hence no delight in inner stillness; no prior practice of insight, hence no delight in clear seeing.
These are a realistic checklist. Most are not exotic meditative problems but ordinary ones: company, teachers, food, sleep, busyness.

quiz.q: How many obstacles to light-perception are there, and how are they divided?
options: eleven — four with reflection-wisdom, seven with cultivation-wisdom
quiz.why: "Eleven things to be remedied: four belonging to light-perception joined with reflection-wisdom, and seven belonging to light-perception joined with cultivation-wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: before calm and insight are achieved, it cannot be called wisdom from cultivation.

quiz.q: When, per Master Cháng Bǎi, does wisdom count as "wisdom from cultivation"?
options: only after achieving calm and insight; before that it is only hearing or reflection wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it should be known that before calm and insight are achieved, it cannot count as wisdom from cultivation — only wisdom from hearing or reflection.

quiz.q: What three kinds of mundane purity does the treatise name?
options: attaining concentration, perfecting it, mastery over it
quiz.why: "What is mundane purity of every kind? In brief, threefold: attaining concentration, perfecting concentration, and mastery over concentration."

quiz.q: How do the masters draw the line between "attaining" and "perfecting" concentration?
options: attaining is access concentration; perfecting is full success in the four form absorptions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: first, attaining concentration means achieving access concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: attaining concentration refers to access concentration; perfecting concentration is complete success in the four form absorptions.

quiz.q: Non-Buddhists also have the absorptions. Where, per Master Cháng Bǎi, do they fall short?
options: they do not care about mastery over concentration or severing affliction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: non-Buddhists also have the four absorptions and eight attainments, but they pay no attention to mastery over concentration or to severing affliction.
